title: Verkhovna Rada appoints Yevhenii Khmara as defense minister
body:
On 19 August 2026, the Verkhovna Rada appointed Yevhenii Khmara, the former acting head of the Security Service of Ukraine, as defense minister. According to Ukrainska Pravda, 312 members of parliament voted in favour. Halyna Mykhailiuk, the President's Representative in the Rada, presented his candidacy. Khmara took the oath from the parliamentary rostrum.

Khmara said he had been discharged from military service under Article 26 of the Law on Military Duty and Military Service, which he described as organisational measures for senior officers. Opposition members objected that they wanted to hear from President Volodymyr Zelensky in person.

On 18 August, Zelensky had submitted nominations for Khmara as defense minister and for Andrii Sybiha as foreign minister. On 19 August, the parliamentary defense committee unanimously backed Khmara, with all 15 members voting in favour. The appointment came after protests supporting former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who had been dismissed in July, had continued for more than a month.
